# Lyra Watch

> Lyra Watch tracks what the media says about politicians, investors, executives and public figures:
> who is named in the news, their job, a 0–100 popularity rating, their documented political
> affiliation, the issues their coverage is about and the companies they are linked to. All data is
> public JSON with stable URLs; link to it freely. It also measures who moves markets: how often a
> company's stock made a big move on the days a person was in the news about it.

## Access and prices

- Free, no key: everything below, with the market record summarised (top 5 of the impact board, each
  person's impact verdict) and the story feed one hour behind.
- Full and real time: send an API key as the `X-Lyra-Key` header (or `Authorization: Bearer lw_...`).
  Requests spend prepaid credits: 1 for a person, 2 for a list or the feed, 5 for the impact board,
  10 for live events. Every response carries `X-Lyra-Credits-Remaining`. With no credits left the API
  answers `402 Payment Required` with the prices. A first key comes with 100 free credits.
- Keys and credit packs: https://lyraauth.com/watch/account/ · prices as JSON:
  https://lyraauth.com/api/watch/account/pricing

## Data (JSON, no key needed)

- [People index](https://lyraauth.com/api/watch/people): everyone the coverage names who has a Wikipedia article or is on the watchlist. Query parameters: `q` (search name, job or company), `watched=true|false`, `ticker` (e.g. `NVDA`: people whose coverage names that listed company), `limit` (up to 500).
- [One person](https://lyraauth.com/api/watch/people/keir-starmer): `/api/watch/people/{id}`, where `id` is the lowercase name with hyphens (e.g. `jensen-huang`, `flavio-bolsonaro`). Fields: `job`, `popularity` {score, tier, basis}, `politics` {parties, offices, basis, source, political_coverage}, `interests` [{topic, share}], `companies`, `tone`, `headlines`, `links`.
- [Story feed](https://lyraauth.com/api/watch/feed.json): JSON Feed 1.1 of the latest headlines, one hour behind the live subscriber stream. Each item lists the people named with links to their JSON records.
- [Watchlist](https://lyraauth.com/api/watch/figures): the tracked politicians, investors, executives and public figures, with disclosed trades and power moves at `/api/watch/figures/{slug}`.
- [Who moves markets](https://lyraauth.com/api/watch/impact): per person, `days` (trading days they were in the news about a listed company), `big_moves` (days the stock moved at least two of its usual daily swings), `big_share` vs `usual_big_share`, `lift` (the ratio) and `verdict`. `?ticker=NVDA` keeps people measured on that stock. Full rows (`by_ticker`, `biggest` days) need a key. It shows what happened on those days, not what caused it.
- Said & traded: with a key, watchlist records carry `said_and_traded`: each disclosed trade with the days in the 30 before and after when they were in the news about that company.
- [Health](https://lyraauth.com/api/watch/health): whether the data is up to date.

- Accounts and posts: each person record has `accounts` (official handles from Wikidata, with `read: true` where Lyra reads the free feed: YouTube, Bluesky, Mastodon, official websites) and, for the watchlist, `posts`: their own recent posts plus news stories about posts on X, Truth Social, Instagram, TikTok and others (`reported: true`; the post may be by or about them).

- Interviews and discussion: watchlist records also carry `interviews` (news interviews, speeches and podcast episodes from the last 30 days) and `discussion` (mentions in the last 24 hours on Hacker News, Bluesky and, where enabled, Reddit, with tone and links to the busiest threads; individual users' posts aren't included).

- Signals: watchlist records carry `court_cases` (US federal cases from the last 30 days naming them as a party, via CourtListener). The live stream also carries Wikipedia edits to tracked people's articles, attention spikes in their Wikipedia readership, and official statements (White House, 10 Downing Street).

## How to read the fields

- `popularity.score` is 70% Wikipedia page views over the last 30 days (log scale) and 30% headline count. It measures attention now, not lifetime fame.
- `politics` holds only documented facts (party membership and current offices from Wikidata or an official source, linked in `source`). Lyra never infers anyone's political views. `political_coverage` is the share of their headlines about elections, taxes, immigration, trade or policy.
- `interests` are the topics their news coverage is about, as a share of their headlines.
- `tone` is a keyword score of their headlines, not a judgement of the person.

## Pages for people

- [Lyra Watch](https://lyraauth.com/watch/): the directory. A person's page is `https://lyraauth.com/watch/#person/{id}`.
- [Lyra Watch Live](https://lyraauth.com/watch/live/): the real-time stream, for subscribers.
